prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage
for the invention of targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional molecules that induce proximity to the ubiquitin ligase machinery

statement.case_for: Both parts pass my physicist's test of a clear underlying principle that opened a capability that did not exist before. Base editing is a defined chemical reaction, deamination of a displaced DNA strand by an evolved deaminase positioned by a catalytically impaired Cas protein, which gives single-nucleotide change without a double-strand break. It is independently reproduced, already in the clinic, and has a stable core concept since 2016-2017. Targeted protein degradation replaces occupancy-driven inhibition with event-driven, catalytic removal of a target through induced proximity. The principle is simple and quantitative (ternary-complex cooperativity), the chemistry is molecular design, and it is the candidate that the most members, five, place in their top three. Pairing them gives the committee two distinct, explainable stories in chemical biology that a broad audience can follow, each with a tight and defensible set of names, and the union stays at three people.
statement.case_against: Base editing follows the 2020 prize for CRISPR-Cas9 and could be read as an extension of genome editing rather than a separate field. Its credit is also contestable: Komor and Gaudelli were the lead experimentalists and Kondo and Nishida reported a parallel deaminase approach (Target-AID), so a Liu-only citation will be challenged. Degraders have strong mechanistic confirmation, but clinical validation is still accumulating, and a PROTAC prize would leave out Ciulli and the cereblon/molecular glue strand of Handa, Ito and Gray, which is an arguably separate discovery. Putting two chemical-biology achievements together also narrows the prize to one corner of chemistry, whereas B008 and B037 are core chemistry with cleaner attribution.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks Car-Parrinello first as a clean two-person prize with unambiguous priority and four decades of validation, and he prefers a Liu-led base editing configuration given the 2020 CRISPR prize.
responses.response: I agree that Car and Parrinello have the cleanest attribution of any candidate, and I take his point that Liu is the natural centre of base editing, which is why I have narrowed my own preferred part to Liu alone rather than my opening trio. I do not accept that the 2020 prize makes base editing derivative. Cas9 cuts, whereas base editors perform a different, chemically defined reaction, and the difference in mechanism is what I would put in the citation. I also ask him what the committee gains by choosing a method-development prize over one that reached patients; I will keep B037 in view as a possible companion if the group wants a computational part, but it was ranked first by one member and I see no broad support yet.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first as a mechanistically clear deamination chemistry with clinical use, and ranks sequencing-by-synthesis second as an overdue, chemically grounded invention by Balasubramanian and Klenerman.
responses.response: We agree on base editing. I now depart from the three-name Liu, Komor, Gaudelli trio that he and I both proposed in the opening. On reflection, Komor and Gaudelli were first authors in the Liu laboratory, and including them invites an argument about Kondo and Nishida that the committee cannot settle cleanly, so I now prefer a single laureate and a citation about the method. On sequencing, I accept the chemistry is real and the maturity is not in doubt, but the credit among Balasubramanian, Klenerman, Rothberg, Mayer and Ju is the problem; I would want him to explain why Solexa chemistry should be set apart from pyrosequencing before I move it above the degraders.

responses.point: Aili ranks PROTAC degradation first as a clear case of molecular design principles changing what chemists and clinicians can do, and proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, noting that the cereblon glue strand would be hard to fit into three names.
responses.response: I largely agree and this is why B028 is my second part. Where I differ is on Ciulli: his VHL ligands and ternary-complex work were decisive for making degraders drug-like, but the original concept and first demonstrations belong to Crews and Deshaies, and keeping the PROTAC part at two names lets the prize carry Liu without exceeding three people. I would like to hear whether he thinks the committee can defend omitting Ciulli, and how he would justify setting cereblon aside, since Handa and Ito explain the thalidomide mechanism, which is a different finding that the citation must not appear to claim.

responses.point: Zou ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first, calling it an enabling method with very high originality and lasting impact, noting that Kosugi's stoichiometric tin chemistry is a precursor and that the 2010 cross-coupling prize did not cover amination.
responses.response: This is the strongest challenge to my configuration. Buchwald and Hartwig give a two-person prize with long validation and, as he says, overdue recognition, and the ligand design is real chemistry. My hesitation is generative potential: it is a superb enabling method, but for a broad audience it delivers less that is unforeseen than the two chemical-biology parts I propose. I list it as my first alternative rather than ignoring it, and I would support it as a second part if the committee wants a synthesis prize beside base editing, since two names plus Liu fit within three.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular condensates first as a new physical-chemical principle of cellular organisation, with phase diagrams and saturation concentrations, while acknowledging that the generality of in-cell phase separation is still debated.
responses.response: As a physicist I am drawn to the thermodynamic framing and I rank it fifth. My concern is the one she names herself: it is not yet clear how much of intracellular organisation is demixing, and the quantitative evidence in cells is harder to separate from other assemblies. Three names are also tight, with Pappu and Mittag making real contributions to sequence-encoded theory. I keep it as my second alternative and would ask her what measurement would settle whether the principle is general.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can defend crediting Liu alone for base editing given the contributions of Komor and Gaudelli and the parallel Kondo and Nishida work.
Whether a PROTAC citation should be limited to Crews and Deshaies, or whether Ciulli and the cereblon strand require separate treatment.
Clinical maturity of degraders and long-term safety of base editors, where I rely on general knowledge rather than current trial data.
Whether pairing two chemical-biology achievements is the right balance against a core-chemistry part such as B008 or B037.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile: none of the shortlisted candidates is at Lund, in NanoLund, or a known collaborator. I note that Peter Somfai and Emma Sparr are Lund colleagues, but that is not a conflict with any shortlisted candidate.
